nodes.summary: For every family of groups $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ none of which contains a generalized torsion element (an element $h \ne 1$ such that some nonempty product of conjugates of $h$ is trivial), the free product of the family contains no generalized torsion element.
nodes.title: Free products of groups without generalized torsion have no generalized torsion

nodes.summary: The statement that for every family of groups $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ none of which contains a generalized torsion element (an element $h \ne 1$ such that some nonempty product of conjugates of $h$ is trivial), the free product of the family contains no generalized torsion element either.
nodes.title: Kopytov–Medvedev question on generalized torsion in free products (Kourovka 16.49)

nodes.summary: An element $h$ of a group $H$ is a generalized torsion element if $h \ne 1$ and there are $n \ge 1$ elements $x_1, \dots, x_n \in H$, not necessarily distinct, such that $(x_1^{-1} h x_1)(x_2^{-1} h x_2) \cdots (x_n^{-1} h x_n) = 1$.
nodes.title: Generalized torsion elements (Kourovka 16.48)

nodes.summary: An element $h$ of a group $H$ is a generalized torsion element when $h \ne 1$ and some nonempty product of conjugates of $h$ is trivial, that is, $x_1^{-1} h x_1 \cdots x_k^{-1} h x_k = 1$ for some $k \ge 1$ and some $x_1, \dots, x_k \in H$.
nodes.title: Generalized torsion element (Kourovka 16.49)

nodes.summary: The Kopytov–Medvedev proposition is false: there is a group $H$ with no generalized torsion element that admits no right order.
nodes.title: Some group without generalized torsion is not right-orderable (Kourovka 16.48)

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that every group $H$ with no generalized torsion element is right-orderable, that is, admits a right order.
nodes.title: The Kopytov–Medvedev question (Kourovka 16.48)

nodes.summary: The right orders of a group $G$ are the binary relations $\preceq$ on $G$ that are linear orders (reflexive, transitive, antisymmetric and total) and are invariant under right multiplication: $a \preceq b$ implies $ac \preceq bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.
nodes.title: Right orders on a group (Kourovka 16.48)
